title: plugin-audit: a failed DDL for an audit table at boot is logged at warn and the boot stays green
body:
## Background

`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts:541-545` (`provisionSystemTables`, on `main`) loops over `SysAuditLog`, `SysActivity`, `SysComment` and `SysCommentReaction`. When an object's `syncObjectSchema` throws, it logs `AuditPlugin: could not provision ${obj.name} storage — …` at **`warn`** and continues.

## Governing text

AGENTS.md, "Degradation log levels — `warn` vs `error`": "**Durability / data-consistency degradation → `error`.** … DDL that was supposed to run did not … Nothing looks broken; the loss surfaces a release later". An `error` there owes ① the consequence and ② the fix, both in its first line.

## Evidence that this is not hypothetical

The merge-queue build 38185050868 (#22895) failed one test. `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.telemetry-sibling.integration.test.ts:209` found exactly one audit table missing after a green `serve` boot: `os migrate plan` listed `create_table:sys_activity`, while `sys_audit_log` was present.
- It did not reproduce: 15 of 15 runs passed on the merge and 15 of 15 on `main` alone, including under concurrent load (#15204 comment 6115811655).
- The only site found that can leave one of these tables absent with the boot green is this `warn`.
- The test spawns `serve` with `spawnSync` and does not print its output, so the CI log can neither confirm nor refute the line.

## The problem

When an audit table's DDL fails, for example on a busy SQLite file, the deployment runs with no `sys_activity` (or `sys_audit_log`) table. It looks healthy, and audit and activity writes have nowhere to land. Per the rule above this is a durability degradation, so it should be `error`, not `warn`.

## Asked of the fix

- Log at `error`, once, with the consequence (which audit table is not durable, and that the system keeps looking healthy) and the fix (what restores it, for example `os migrate apply`, or the opt-out that makes it deliberate). Or fail the boot, if that is the policy for core audit storage.
- A pin that a forced `syncObjectSchema` failure on one audit object produces that `error` line.
- Optional, for the next occurrence: the integration test above prints the `serve` child's stderr on failure, so a recurrence names its cause.

Found while root-causing the #22895 dequeue (stage W of #15204). Not part of #15204.
